page: Microsoft Azure D48als_v7 is an x86_64 compute-optimized server belonging to the Dalsv7 family. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. It does not include bundled local storage or dedicated GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable. The virtualization layer is managed by Microsoft Hyper-V.

In benchmark testing, the AMD EPYC processor demonstrates top-tier single-core and multi-core CPU performance. Single-core stress-ng and Geekbench scores rank in the top 10%, aided by the high clock speed and advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and vector neural network instructions. Memory performance is strong for small-block cached reads and large-block writes, though large-block uncached read bandwidth sits in the average tier. Cryptographic and compression tasks, such as AES encryption and single-threaded gzip decompression, also register top-tier performance.

Given the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this instance is optimized for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. It is highly suitable for software compilation, ray tracing, text and image processing, and web serving. It also handles small-model LLM inference efficiently, though performance scales down to average for larger models. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and high clock speed deliver strong compute density per resource unit, making it a viable choice for CPU-bound tasks where local storage is not required.
